title: kv-cache: improved memory management and eviction (fragmentation, paging, spillover)
author: Priya Singh
description: Context and motivation: We observed increased KV cache fragmentation and out-of-memory-like spill events on long-running GPU inference workers serving long-tail conversational workloads. This PR implements a set of coordinated improvements to KV cache memory management and eviction to reduce fragmentation, enable efficient paging/spillover, and provide safer fallbacks when device memory pressure spikes. Goals: 1) reduce sustained GPU memory fragmentation over time, 2) keep latency SLOs during partial spills by prioritizing active entries, 3) enable configurable spill targets (CPU RAM or local SSD) and fast background compaction, and 4) add observability to track fragmentation and spill churn. Summary of changes: - Introduced page-based allocation layer for KV cache with fixed-size pages and per-bucket free lists to reduce external fragmentation. Pages are tracked by allocation age and live-entry density. - Implemented a size-aware eviction policy (LRU-Size) that biases eviction towards cold large entries to free contiguous pages for compaction. The policy is tunable via runtime config flags. - Added in-place background defragmentation/compaction that copies hot entries into new contiguous pages while holding minimal locks to avoid blocking inference threads. Compaction runs at low priority and can be throttled by CPU quota. - Implemented spillover pipeline: pages can be relocated to host RAM or optionally to local SSD. Spill targets are pluggable; the default is host RAM with an async IO path for SSD. Metrics and thresholds control when pages are selected for spill. - Provided safe fast-path for inference when a required KV page is spilled: on-demand fetch with speculative decoding and prefetch hints to reduce stall time. - Extended evictor to prefer contiguous page releases to reduce fragmentation and accelerate subsequent allocations. - Added detailed metrics: kv_pages_total, kv_pages_free, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_spill_ops/sec, kv_spill_latency_p50/p95, kv_compaction_bytes/sec, kv_eviction_size_histogram. - Updated config flags and operator docs with recommended defaults for hosted vs dedicated deployments. - Added unit and integration tests, and a micro-benchmark harness for long-tail chat workloads. Checklist: - [x] Page allocator implementation and tests - [x] LRU-Size eviction + tuning knobs - [x] Background compaction + safety checks - [x] Spillover to host RAM and SSD path - [x] Observability and dashboards - [x] Perf microbenchmarks and CI perf job - [x] Documentation updates References: Linear ENG-4721 (kv cache fragmentation), ENG-4815 (spillover design); related PRs: pr-25701, pr-24690. Performance results: On our perf canary for a 12B model with long-tail chat traces (90th percentile seq lengths), this change reduced sustained GPU memory fragmentation ratio from ~0.37 to ~0.08 and reduced OOM-related spill events by 92%. End-to-end median latency impact: +2-4% under heavy compaction load (configurable), but 95th/99th percentile latency improved by 20-35% due to fewer async stall-and-recover sequences. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind kv_cache_v2_enable. Start with canary on dedicated pool, run for 72h, then progressively enable for additional pools. Backout: feature flag off or set spill target to none. Migration notes: existing caches are compatible; an on-start compaction run will be triggered the first time the new allocator is enabled (cost is measurable but bounded).

review_comments: Ethan Liu: Can you clarify how the page size was chosen and whether it's workload dependent? Reply: We picked 64KB pages based on empirical tradeoffs between fragmentation and copy overhead; the page size is configurable via KV_PAGE_SIZE and we included a benchmark that sweeps this value.

Marco Alvarez: Background compaction holding locks worried me. How do you ensure tail latency doesn't regress? Reply: Compaction uses a try-lock pattern and bounded work per cycle; if try-lock fails we skip and reschedule. We also added a low-priority execution class and CPU throttle knob.

Samantha Ko: SSD spill path needs safety for degraded IO. What are fallbacks? Reply: SPI ll path is optional; if IO errors exceed threshold we switch to host RAM spill and emit an alert. We also added a config to disable SSD for cloud instances without ephemeral SSDs.
Ethan Liu: Could we get more metrics for compaction churn? Reply: Added kv_compaction_bytes/sec and compaction_attempts counter; dashboards updated.
Marco Alvarez: minor nit on naming and a unit test flake. Addressed in force-push.
Samantha Ko: Approved after validating perf numbers and reviewing tests.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: page-based allocator, size-aware eviction, background compaction, and configurable spillover to host RAM/SSD. Reduces fragmentation and OOM-related spill events for long-tail chat workloads. Feature-flagged (kv_cache_v2_enable).
